question: Can six knots with seven simple meetings and at most one extra opening per knot produce a whole closure in the first four ordinary cuts?
forbidden_inputs: No paid cuts after four on any new six-knot founder; no donor funding or sign substitution; no rank or isomorphism shortcut silently changes source mass.
primary_observable: All coverage, global shortages, actual paid births and whole closures; attached odd product checks at actual closure; all initially and still-connected live groups and their observed fates; both exact labelled weightings.
cheapest_meaningful_control: Enumerate seven-pair subsets and separately tree-plus-two-edits, verify every named multiplicity and flag orbit; native and witnessed physical rosters; matched one-deletion replays and old even vs supplied odd signs.
first_executable_signal: Enumerate all connected seven-meeting patterns, generate the decorated sources and compare spanning-tree counts and physical growth under both supplied laws.
resource_budget: Six founders, seven meetings, 64 decorations, at most four paid cuts on each new source; one CPU thread and six GiB per process. Register any projected individual run over ten minutes.
stop_rule: Complete the four-cut population, state both ranked positive minima or their absence, and provide a class ledger for every connected live survivor. Mathematical continuations only from a structural invariant or exact return visible at those four cuts.
decision_or_followup_rule: Mark any unresolved later fate by founder, full eligible denominator and missing invariant. Use GO or STOP for the selected next direction and report the pending scientific referee independently of design approval.
